title: Grants & Scholarships for Single Moms Going Back to School
summary: Discover grants, scholarships, and financial aid for single moms going back to school, including federal, state, and private opportunities.
body_markdown:
Single moms going back to school can get thousands of dollars in grants that never have to be paid back through federal grants, private scholarships, workforce training funds, and state programs.


This support can help lower the significant financial burden of paying for school alongside housing, childcare, and all the other expenses single moms face.


Let’s look at grant and scholarship options for single mothers returning to school, from nonprofits to federal and state programs.


We also give tips for writing a winning application and backup options if gift aid doesn't cover the full bill.


## Scholarships for Single Moms Going Back to School


Most of the funding on this list comes from nonprofits, foundations, and private companies. Several let you use the money for childcare and rent, not just tuition.


The amount available, the requirements, and the deadlines can shift from year to year, so recheck all the details before you apply.


If the application deadline has passed for this funding cycle, it will usually reopen at a set time, so you can find that out as well.


### [Stepful Grants](https://www.stepful.com/grants)


- **Organization:** Stepful, an online healthcare education provider
- **Amount:** Varies by student and program
- **Deadline:** Rolling, no fixed application window
- **Application:** Fill out a simple online form


Here at Stepful, we offer[need-based grants](https://www.stepful.com/grants#:~:text=Employer-,Stepful%20funding,-At%20Stepful%2C%20we%27re) that lower tuition for students paying out of pocket.


We also help students access workforce board money, employer tuition benefits, and[military-related funding](https://www.stepful.com/post/programs-for-military-members-spouses-to-get-free-healthcare-training-certifications) .


These funds can be used across[Stepful's healthcare programs](https://www.stepful.com/programs) , including online courses for medical assistants, pharmacy technicians, dental assistants, and more.


Applying is easy since there is no essay or FAFSA required. Just fill out a short[application](https://www.stepful.com/) , and you will see if you qualify for a need-based grant.


If you are active-duty military or are a military spouse, check the box on the application and a Stepful adviser will walk you through the process.


[Learn about Stepful's 5-Month Online Medical Assistant Program](https://www.stepful.com/medical-assistant)


[Explore Program](https://www.stepful.com/medical-assistant)


### [Live Your Dream Award](https://www.soroptimist.org/our-work/live-your-dream-awards/apply-for-the-live-your-dream-awards.html)


- **Organization:** Soroptimist International of the Americas
- **Amount:** $1,000 is the average “club level” grant. Each club's first-place recipient is then eligible for a $3,000 or $5,000 region-level award, and regional winners are eligible for up to $10,000 at the international level. One recipient can receive up to $16,000 across all three.
- **Deadline:** Nov. 15, 2026. Applications opened Aug. 1.
- **Application:** Includes an essay about your experiences and goals in your own words


This award goes to women who provide the primary financial support for themselves and their dependents and who are enrolled in or accepted to a vocational/skills training or undergraduate degree program. Funds can cover tuition, books, transportation, or childcare.


You cannot already hold a graduate degree or be pursuing one. You cannot have previously received a Live Your Dream or Women’s Opportunity Award. See their website for all the eligibility details.


### [Patsy Takemoto Mink Education Support Award](https://www.patsyminkfoundation.org/education-support-application)


- **Organization:** Patsy Takemoto Mink Education Foundation
- **Amount:** Up to $5,000, with five awards given each cycle
- **Deadline:** The 2026-27 cycle closed Aug. 1, 2026. Details for the next cycle will be posted in May 2027.
- **Application:** Covers financial need, personal circumstances, educational path, vocational goals, and civic engagement


These awards were created for low-income women with minor children who are pursuing education or training. You can use funds for educational and living expenses.


You must be at least 17 yourself and enrolled full-time at an accredited, not-for-profit U.S. program or institution. The 2026-27 income limits were $21,640 for a family of two, $27,320 for a family of three, and $33,000 for a family of four. You can find all the eligibility details on their website.


### [Jeannette Rankin National Scholar Grant](https://rankinfoundation.org/national-scholar-grant/)


- **Organization:** Jeannette Rankin Foundation
- **Amount:** Up to $2,500 a year, renewable for up to five years
- **Deadline:** The 2025-26 cycle closed Feb. 13, 2026, and no new opening date has been posted yet. The last cycle opened Nov. 3, so watch the site this fall.
- **Application:** Requires an eligibility survey, an application that takes about 90 minutes, essay responses submitted through Submittable, and recommendation letters


This grant is unrestricted, non-tuition support for women and nonbinary students 35 and older with demonstrated financial need who are pursuing technical or vocational education, an associate’s degree, or a first bachelor's degree at an accredited U.S. school.


### [A Grandmother's Love Single Mom Scholarship](https://bold.org/scholarships/a-grandmothers-love-single-mom-scholarship/)


- **Organization:** Privately funded through Bold.org
- **Amount:** $550, one winner
- **Deadline:** Sept. 30, 2026, with the winner announced Oct. 31
- **Application:** Requires a 500–700-word essay on the difficulties you face as a single mom in school, plus a photo of you with your children


Open to single mothers enrolled as undergraduate or graduate students with a 2.7 GPA or higher. The award is small, but the application is easy, and awards this size draw far fewer applicants than the big national ones.


### [Organic Formula Shop Single Parent Scholarship](https://organicformulashop.com/pages/single-parent-scholarship)


- **Organization:** Organic Formula Shop
- **Amount:** $2,000, awarded twice a year
- **Deadline:** Twice a year on a rolling basis; Spring semester deadline is Nov. 10, 2026
- **Application:** Includes an essay of 500-1,000 words explaining why you should be chosen


Single parents enrolled at a four-year, two-year, vocational, or technical institution in the U.S. can apply. You must be a U.S. citizen or permanent legal resident. Every field of study qualifies, and there is no GPA requirement.


### [Helping Hands for Single Moms Scholarships](https://helpinghandsforsinglemoms.org/apply/)


- **Organization:** Helping Hands for Single Moms
- **Amount:** Varies
- **Deadline:** Rolling
- **Application:** An online application and essay


This program serves single moms in Arizona, specifically Maricopa County and the greater Phoenix metro area. However, similar chapters in Dallas and Houston, TX, are called[Single Mom Scholars](https://singlemomscholars.org/) .


Applicants must be single or divorced, not living with a domestic partner, with at least one child living with them who is in 12th grade or younger. Your household income must be at or below 150% of federal poverty guidelines.


You need to have completed at least one semester of college with nine credit hours. You must continue to carry nine or more credit hours per semester and have a cumulative 2.8 GPA or higher.


### [P.E.O. Program for Continuing Education](https://www.peointernational.org/educational-support/program-for-continuing-education/eligibility-and-application-process/)


- **Organization:** P.E.O. International
- **Amount:** Up to $4,000, awarded once
- **Deadline:** No fixed date. Chapters sponsor applicants year-round, but a recommendation has to reach P.E.O. at least four to 10 weeks before your program starts.
- **Application:** Requires sponsorship by a local P.E.O. chapter, followed by an online application you have 30 days to complete with income and expense documentation


P.E.O. (Philanthropic Educational Organization) provides grants for women whose education stopped and then restarted. You need at least 24 consecutive months as a non-student somewhere in your adult life, and you must be within 18 months of finishing your program.


Certificate and technical programs count, not just degrees, and the money can go toward childcare, transportation, uniforms, and testing fees. If you don't know anyone in P.E.O., the site has a form for requesting sponsorship.


## Grants & Federal Aid for Single Moms Returning to School


Federal and state grants are a major source of funding for parents returning to school, and like scholarships, they don't have to be repaid.


Almost all of them are need-based, which works in your favor when you're supporting children on one income.


The first step is filling out the[Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)](https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa) . The 2027-28 FAFSA[opens up](https://financialaidtoolkit.ed.gov/tk/announcement-detail.jsp?id=fafsa-updates) by October 1, 2026.


Even if you think you might earn too much to qualify for federal grants, it’s still worth filling out because states, schools, and outside programs use it to determine their own awards. FAFSA is also required to see which federal student loans you qualify for.


### Federal Pell Grant


The Pell Grant is the biggest federal gift-aid program for undergraduates. For the[2026-27 award year](https://fsapartners.ed.gov/knowledge-center/library/dear-colleague-letters/2026-01-30/2026-27-federal-pell-grant-maximum-and-minimum-award-amounts) , the maximum is $7,395, and the minimum is $740.


What you receive depends on your school's cost of attendance, whether you're enrolled full-time or part-time, and your Student Aid Index.


The Student Aid Index is a number calculated from your FAFSA application based on your income and family size. Your school subtracts that number from its cost of attendance to find your financial need. A lower index means more need and more aid, and it can go below zero.


If your children get more than half their support from you, the FAFSA counts you as an[independent student](https://studentaid.gov/apply-for-aid/fafsa/filling-out/dependency) . Your parents' income stays off the form entirely, no matter your age.


Pell also just got bigger in scope. Starting July 1, 2026, the new[Workforce Pell Grant](https://www.ed.gov/about/news/press-release/us-department-of-education-issues-final-rule-create-new-workforce-pell-grant-program) lets students use Pell money for short-term job training programs, some running as little as eight weeks.


Governors, working with their state workforce boards, identify qualifying high-demand fields, and programs must meet completion and employment benchmarks. Because of these changes, more short healthcare certificate programs may now be covered.


To apply, submit the FAFSA. There is no separate Pell application.


### Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant (FSEOG)


FSEOG is a grant for undergraduates with exceptional financial need. Awards range from[$100 to $4,000 a year](https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/grants/fseog) . Each school's financial aid office awards it, but not every school participates.


Timing matters more here than with Pell. Each participating school gets a fixed pot of FSEOG money each year, and once it's gone, no more awards are given out that year. So, completing your FAFSA early is important for this one.


You have to be an undergraduate without a prior bachelor's degree, and eligibility is re-established each year through the FAFSA.


### Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF)


[TANF](https://www.usa.gov/welfare-benefits) is a federally funded, state-run program for low-income families with children. It helps with food, housing, home energy, and childcare, and many states also use TANF dollars to pay for job training and education.


Every state, territory, and participating tribe writes its own rules, so what's covered in Arizona may not match what's covered in Ohio. You have to be a resident of the state where you apply.


[Find your local office](https://acf.gov/ofa/map/about/help-families) through the Administration for Children and Families and ask directly about education and training support.


### Workforce Innovation & Opportunity Act (WIOA) Funding


WIOA is a federal law that funds the[Adult and Dislocated Worker Program](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/workforce-investment/adult) . This program pays for career services and job training for low-income individuals, people receiving public assistance, and those who are basic skills deficient. Many single moms qualify.


Many states and counties offer this[funding for healthcare training](https://www.stepful.com/post/free-healthcare-training-certifications) because regional demand is high.


Stepful accepts[local workforce board funding](https://www.stepful.com/grants) across its programs. These programs are fast and affordable, so tuition may be completely covered for students.


WIOA funding is distributed locally, so the process and the approved training list vary by county. You can start career exploration at an[American Job Center](https://www.careeronestop.org/LocalHelp/AmericanJobCenters/american-job-centers.aspx) .


### Childcare Assistance Programs


States and territories receive federal money through the Childcare and Development Fund to help low-income families pay for childcare so parents can work or attend school.


Income limits and rules differ in every state.[ChildCare.gov](https://childcare.gov/consumer-education/get-help-paying-for-child-care/child-care-financial-assistance-options) lets you select your state and pull up the local program and application steps.


The same page lists other ways to cut childcare costs: Head Start and Early Head Start for children from birth to age 5, state-funded prekindergarten for ages 3 to 5, sibling and military discounts from providers, and dependent care flexible spending accounts through an employer.


### State-Specific Grants for Single Parents


Some states offer funds for single parents or adult learners. Check your state's higher education agency and your state workforce agency to see what your state offers.


Here are two examples:


The[Arkansas Single Parent Scholarship Fund](https://aspsf.org/scholarships/) awards $400 to $1,600 per semester depending on how many credit hours you take, and it covers certificates and trade training as well as degrees. Household income must be under 250% of the federal poverty guidelines.


The list of counties served and application deadlines can be found on the website. There are three application windows per year that are a month long. The next window is Jan. 1 – Feb. 1, 2027.


The[Michigan Achievement Skills Scholarship](https://www.michigan.gov/mistudentaid/programs/michigan-achievement-scholarship/career-training) pays up to $2,000 a year for two years toward career training. You must have been a Michigan resident for at least the past year, finished high school or earned an equivalency certificate in 2023 or later, and enroll within 15 months of that date. There is no age limit, and you do not need to fill out the FAFSA.


## Tips: Applying for Scholarships & Grants as a Single Mom


To make the most of your application time, you will want to be strategic, thoughtful, and get all the details right the first time. Here are some tips that can help you win:


- **File the FAFSA first, and file it early.** Several programs on this list either require it or use it to verify need, and campus-based aid like FSEOG disappears once a school's allocation runs out.
- **Don’t ignore small scholarships and grants.** A $500 local award with a short essay may take an hour and have only dozens of applicants. A $10,000 national award may take a full weekend and draws thousands, so think about where you have the best odds of winning.
- **Look at your county, not just your state.** Community foundations and local United Way chapters often administer small education funds for single parents, and they draw far fewer applicants than a national award does. Search your county name plus "community foundation scholarship" to see what’s available.
- **Include your plan to meet your goals.** Reviewers want to see the plan. Who watches your kids during clinical hours, how you'll cover the tuition gap, what the credential leads to, and what it pays.
- **Be specific and be honest.** Reviewers are reading through stacks of essays that start to sound alike. Being real is one way to cut through.
- **Reuse your essays.** Most prompts are versions of the same two or three questions. Keep a master document and adapt it rather than starting over each time.
- **Track the cycles.** The bigger awards run on fixed calendars. Live Your Dream closes Nov. 15, Patsy Mink posts details in May, and Jeannette Rankin's last cycle opened in early November. Put them in your calendar now with alerts to remind you.
- **Ask your school's financial aid office what they have.** Institutional grants and emergency funds are rarely posted anywhere public, so you have to ask to find out.
- **Don't skip awards that pay for things besides tuition.** Money for childcare, transportation, or books frees up cash you would otherwise have to borrow.
- **Never pay a fee to apply.** Legitimate scholarships don't charge for applications or for "processing" an award.


## Other Financial Aid Options for Single Moms Going Back to School


Gift aid doesn't always cover the whole bill. If there's a gap after grants and scholarships, work through these in order.


### Employer Tuition Assistance


If you're working, ask HR what's available before you borrow. Healthcare employers in particular fund certificates and degrees for staff, and some pay upfront rather than reimbursing you later.


Stepful accepts[employer-sponsored payment](https://www.stepful.com/grants#explore-grants) and will invoice an employer directly if that's how the benefit works.


### Tax Credits


The[Lifetime Learning Credit](https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/education-credits-aotc-and-llc) is worth up to $2,000 per tax return and covers courses taken to acquire or improve job skills, with no requirement that you be pursuing a degree. Note that it is non-refundable, so it can’t reduce your taxable income below $0. For single filers, it phases out between $80,000 and $90,000 in modified adjusted gross income as of the 2025 tax year.


The[American Opportunity Tax Credit](https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/education-credits-aotc-and-llc) offers up to $2,500 annually per eligible student during the first four years of higher education, with up to $1,000 potentially refundable. Income limits apply, and students must attend an eligible school at least half-time while pursuing a degree or recognized credential.


The[Child and Dependent Care Credit](https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/child-and-dependent-care-credit-information) and the[Earned Income Tax Credit](https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/earned-income-tax-credit-eitc) are also worth reviewing before you do your taxes. Neither pays tuition directly, but both can put money back in your pocket.


### Federal Student Loans


If you qualify, you should exhaust all your[federal student loan options](https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/loans) before turning to private student loans.


They have more flexible[repayment options](https://studentaid.gov/manage-loans/repayment/plans) , the potential for[student loan forgiveness](https://studentaid.gov/manage-loans/forgiveness-cancellation) , and borrower protections that private lenders don't offer. The FAFSA determines which ones you qualify for, so there's no separate application.


Remember that all student loans have to be repaid, with interest, even if you don't finish the program.


Be aware that federal aid like Pell and FSEOG only works at schools that participate in federal student aid programs.


### Private Student Loans


Private loans come from banks and credit unions and are generally a last resort. Interest rates are usually higher, and terms are less forgiving.


If you go this route,[compare rates](https://www.credible.com/private-student-loans/prequal/role) , understand the full cost of your loan, and understand how repayment will work.
